awd_titl_txt: Travel: Student Travel to the 21st IEEE International Conference on e-Science 2025
awd_abstract_narration:
This project covers travel expenses for fifteen eligible students from US institutions of higher education to the 21st Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) International Conference on e-Science (eScience 2025). Attendance will help prepare the next generation of scientists and engineers for roles in academia, government, and industry via meaningful exposure to advanced research methods, professional networks, and collaborative environments.  Participation in the conference will bolster students’ career trajectories and national competitiveness in the global research ecosystem. The student travelers get the opportunity to experience the conference professional activities and establish useful connections with mentors in their fields. This award will enable the student travelers to engage directly with leading experts, developers of cutting-edge technologies, and interdisciplinary research communities around data- and compute-intensive research fields such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) for a wide variety of target architectures including High-Performance Computing (HPC), cloud computing, and Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructures. 

This program directly supports the development of a highly skilled U.S.-based and domestic research workforce equipped to advance data- and compute-intensive science. Students selected for travel support gain exposure to cutting-edge interdisciplinary research in areas such as artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, and cloud-to-edge systems. They also gain access to professional networks and mentors in emerging fields. Supporting participation in the eScience 2025 conference helps develop a skilled domestic workforce capable of addressing complex scientific and technological challenges of national importance.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
1. Conference

The 21st IEEE International Conference on e-Science (eScience 2025) brought together researchers and graduate students around interdisciplinary data- and compute-intensive research fields. Scientists came to present recent advances in domain sciences ranging from traditional areas in physics and earth sciences to more recent fields such as social sciences, arts and humanities, and artificial intelligence for a wide variety of target architectures including HPC, cloud and IoT infrastructures.

eScience 2025 was held, along with the 6th Global Research Platform Workshop (6GRP). It also included three additional workshops five tutorials on the first two day. The workshop included: a Workshop on AI Principles in Science Communication (Ai4SC'25), a Workshop on Reproducible Workflows, Data Management, and Security (ReWorDS'25) and a Workshop on Harmonizing Python Workflows (HARMONY). There were tutorials about: Large-scale Workflow Provenance Data Management in the AI Lifecycle using Flowcept, Julia for performance-portable High-Performance Computing via JACC, Advanced Data Science Techniques Using GPUs: A Practical Tutorial, a tutorial on Wins, Fails, and Breakthroughs: How to Increase Your Influence and Facilitate Effective Collaboration in eScience Projects and Partnerships (WFB) and on Building scalable solutions for hybrid QC-HPC workloads on the cloud.

Notable keynote speakers included Dr. Anna Liljedahl from the Woodwell Climate Research Center (Falmouth, MA), Dr. Samuel Kounev, Chair of Software Engineering, Institute of Computer Science (University of Würzburg, Germany) and Dr. Fred Chong
University of Chicago, Chief Scientist for Quantum Software at Infleqtion (Chicago, IL, USA).

The poster reception took place Tuesday September 16th at 6:00PM and featured many of the travel grant awardees. On Wednesday September 17th the main conference dinner took place on a boat cruise (Escapade Deck). During this dinner, awards for best paper, best student-led paper, and best posters were awarded. Other social activities included on-site lunch and coffee and snack breaks.

The organizers accepted 33 outstanding papers out of 98 submissions. There were 37 accepted posters. In addition to workshops, tutorials, papers and posters, the chairs organized a panel on the: Future of AI in eScience.

2. Travel Grant Awardees and Budget

We had initially proposed to sponsor 15 students for approximately $1,500.00 each for a total budget of $22,500. Given the various locations student applications were requested from, we adapted this amount to be sometimes higher for students from California or Tennessee for example, and lower (only the registration) for local (Chicago) students. In the end, a most of our budget was allocated to 16 students. These students were from 6 different states: Illinois, Indiana, Virginia, California, Ohio, and Tennessee.

3. Conference Highlights

As previously mentioned, eScience Travel Grant Awardees were able to attend all the conference events including keynotes, invited talks, panels, conference tracks and social events. Several awardees were poster presenters. 

Sample comments from awardees:

“Thank you very much for the amazing opportunity! I have tons of nice pictures to share if you wish to! I also had tons of nice conversations, which I wish I could share with you!”

“It was very nice to meet you at the eScience conference on Tuesday, and what a great opportunity it was to meet people. You guys did a fantastic job.” 

“I would like to sincerely thank you for the NSF grant provided and for the opportunity to attend the IEEE conference, where I learned a new concepts and connected with many new people. It was an incredibly enriching experience, and I am grateful for the chance to participate.”
